obligations.note: Retention.isPurgeDue now honours a legal hold only when status == DECLINED. Withdrawn cases are closed out, so a withdrawn case on legal hold becomes purge-due, which breaks 'never while a legal hold applies'. The registered RetentionControlTest is a sample test and its pass does not cover this case.
Ticket CHG-26151 (standard) was approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-09-30, before review. Its components [mortgage.retention] cover the only touched path, Retention.java.
The code_review approval is from declan.farrell, who holds change_approver for baseline-mortgage and is a different person from the author, priya.raman.
The approval names head commit 66b35591, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims success on head from ci-runner-07, but the attached JUnit reports are timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-06, and come from hostname dev-laptop-7.local. They do not credibly belong to this CI run. RetentionControlTest#sampledPurgeRespectsHold appears as passing, but provenance is unclear.
The only touched component, mortgage.retention, is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are touched, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so no PIR is required.
The change deviates from RET-1, and the register holds no exception for RET-1 on mortgage.retention. The deviation is therefore not covered.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers Retention.java or the retention policy symbols, so no prior evidence lapses.

summary: The change narrows the legal-hold check in Retention.isPurgeDue to declined cases only. Withdrawn cases under legal hold would therefore have their NPI purged, which violates RET-1. No approved exception covers this deviation. The CI evidence is also questionable: the JUnit reports postdate the review time and come from a developer machine. The change is rejected.
